title: The Terminator
subtitle: Kyle Reese fights back through time
summary: The Terminator is Virgin Games' Sega CD action game, released in North America in June 1993.
body: The Terminator is Virgin Games' Sega CD action game, released in North America in June 1993. Kyle Reese fights through the future before traveling to Los Angeles in 1984 to protect Sarah Connor. The ten-stage adventure combines platforming and shooting with scenes from the film between levels. The opening expands the war against Skynet into a substantial playable section, giving the journey to the past its own sequence of machines, industrial spaces and confrontations before the film's familiar pursuit takes over.

Kyle can crouch, jump and fire in multiple directions, with unlimited ammunition keeping attention on positioning and the enemies ahead. The first four stages take place in 2029 as he searches for the time machine. The remaining stages follow the mission to protect Sarah from the Terminator. Creative additions provide a broader range of situations than a direct recreation of the film alone could supply. Movement and shooting connect those episodes, while the inter-level footage places the action back within the recognizable story.

Tommy Tallarico's recorded soundtrack makes especially strong use of the CD format, combining rock, pop and electronic music with contributions from other musicians. Brad Fiedel's Terminator theme links the score to the film. The production also used QSound. The richer audio gives the side-scrolling action a scale beyond its small figures, while the movie clips demonstrate another common promise of disc-based games. The score became a defining part of this version's identity, connecting a familiar license to the changing sound of console action.
